The key elements of the ‘Rosalind Franklin’ Rover are its advanced drilling system, coupled with a sophisticated on-board science laboratory, and its capability to move autonomously on a variety of terrains on Mars’ surface for at least 218 sols (8 months). Sampling down to a depth of 2 metres significantly increases the probability to detect preserved signs of past or even present life. The so-called “braking engines” will be provided by NASA as Customer Furnished Items (CFIs). The Rover System comprises the ‘Rosalind Franklin’ Rover Module and the Rover Operations Control Centre (ROCC), the latter developed by and located at ALTEC in Torino (Italy), where the ground operations of the Rover surface mission will be performed.
